display.purpose: Hero h1 only, weight 700, two lines max. Runs over the full-bleed hero photograph, never boxed into a column.

title.purpose: Panel and card titles; title-lg for split-section h3, title-sm for compact card headings.

sub.purpose: Card and split-section body copy. The workhorse size below Body.

caption.purpose: Secondary lines inside compact components, such as pipeline step descriptions.

label.purpose: The single mono size (12px, +0.08em, uppercase). Panel headers, provenance labels, telemetry meta. Reserved for data-shaped content: sections carrying no live telemetry use plain sans headings instead.

stat.purpose: Platform-fact figures and metric callouts. Always tabular-nums.

shadows.name: ambient
shadows.purpose: Resting lift for framed product photographs on paper.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Reserved tier; hover feedback brightens borders instead of deepening shadow.

shadows.name: console
shadows.purpose: The hero telemetry card, the one floating surface over the photograph.

shadows.name: product-drop
shadows.purpose: Applied to transparent-PNG hardware renders so they sit on the raised panel rather than float.

motion.name: transition-standard
motion.purpose: Buttons, links, colour and border state changes. The primary CTA scales to 1.02 on hover and dips 1px on press.

motion.name: transition-surface
motion.purpose: Card border and background hover shifts. Surfaces never translate or grow.

motion.name: reveal
motion.value: opacity 0 + y 22px -> resolved, 500ms cubic-bezier(0.21, 0.47, 0.32, 0.98), whileInView once, -70px margin
motion.purpose: Scroll-triggered fade-up for sections and panels. Reduced motion renders static and fully visible via a post-mount swap so hydration still matches the server.

motion.name: count-up
motion.purpose: Platform-fact figures. Reduced motion shows final values immediately with no in-view gating.

motion.name: rail-scroll
motion.value: scrollBy({ behavior: 'smooth' }) with snap-x snap-mandatory and scroll-padding matched to the container gutter
motion.purpose: Industries rail arrow navigation. The scroll-padding is what keeps card one aligned to the container line at rest.

notes: No infinite or ambient animation ships anywhere on the page. Every motion is a one-shot response to scroll or input, which is why the old marquee, chip-float and pulse-dot keyframes were deleted rather than left unused.
Font tokens MUST live in `@theme inline`. A plain `@theme` emits the var() chain onto :root where the next/font variables on <html> cannot resolve, silently dropping every face to the system stack.

narrative.overview: The page is the product. Every surface behaves like a fleet console that never sleeps: telemetry set in mono, status carried by small colored dots, panels divided by hairlines, and one full-bleed photograph above the fold — a drone view of an active earthworks site where a mixed fleet is working, graded into the dark world; the overhead angle is the point, because it is the view the product itself gives you. The grammar is Linear's — quiet neutral labels, hairline-divided panels, tight Archivo, restrained color — worn over Zenduit's own materials: designed navy darks, warm paper lights, and a telemetry palette drawn from the company's real brand family. Chrome stays silent so data can speak. Color is never decoration; it marks something a visitor can click or a vehicle's live condition.
keyCharacteristics: Real photography where it earns its place: the graded hero, Zenduit's own per-industry photos on the rail, and the official hardware renders
Photographs ship unadorned, framed by a hairline and radius, never overlaid or captioned with fake UI status chrome
Frosted glass on dark sections only, and only where content actually passes beneath it
Hairline-divided panel grammar for every feature group
Mono voice (IBM Plex Mono, tabular) reserved for data-shaped content; sections carrying no telemetry use plain sans
Hybrid rhythm: dark cinema at the edges, warm paper for the body
One accent (Zenduit blue) that appears only where something acts
No infinite animation anywhere; every motion is a one-shot response to scroll or input

rules.name: The No-Pill Rule
rules.body: Badges and labels are never pill-shaped containers. A label is type — mono, tracked, colored if it must signal. Circles are reserved for telemetry status dots and nothing else.

rules.name: The Color Earns Its Place Rule
rules.body: Color appears in exactly three roles: interactive elements (links, primary CTA), the brand route/selection accent, and telemetry status dots. Labels, icons, eyebrows, and badges stay neutral.

rules.name: The Two Gradients Rule
rules.body: Exactly two gradient moments exist on the page, the hero scrim and the final CTA panel wash. No other gradients, ever.

rules.name: The Mono-for-Data Rule
rules.body: Every number, unit ID, timestamp, percentage, and status string is IBM Plex Mono with tabular-nums. If it could appear in a terminal, it is mono. If it could not, it is not.

rules.name: The Heading Stands Alone Rule
rules.body: Section headings carry their own weight. No decorative eyebrow above them, and no dot-separated uppercase triads anywhere: that construction reads as machine-generated.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Separation is a 1px low-alpha border before it is ever a shadow. Hover feedback brightens the border and shifts the background tint; nothing translates or grows, with the primary CTA's 1.02 hover scale as the single stated exception.

rules.name: The Verified Proof Rule
rules.body: No customer name, logo, rating, or outcome metric ships unless it is verifiable on zenduit.com or supplied by the client. Unverifiable claims are removed, not softened.

dos: Do set every number, ID, and timestamp in IBM Plex Mono with tabular-nums.
Do build feature groups as hairline-divided panels with a plain heading.
Do let photographs bleed into their own region of a card rather than sitting in a letterboxed strip.
Do keep font tokens in `@theme inline`, or every custom face silently falls back to the system stack.
Do use Zenduit's real product names (ZenCam Plus, ZenTemp, ZenDoor, ZenID, ZenTitan, ZenTurbo, ZenduELD, ZenduConnect).
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion on every animation, including scroll reveals and count-ups.
donts: Don't add gradients beyond the two sanctioned moments.
Don't color labels, eyebrows, icons, or badges: color marks action and telemetry only.
Don't use pill-shaped badges or capsule containers anywhere.
Don't set mono micro-labels in sections that carry no live data.
Don't write em-dashes into visible copy, or dot-separated uppercase triads.
Don't use pure #fff or #000; the neutrals are designed.
Don't invent a type size: the ramp is a closed set, not a suggestion.
Don't ship a customer name, rating, or metric that cannot be verified.
